authority.note: This packet frames required adversarial reviews; script generation never answers or decides them.

limitations: Evidence context is assembled mechanically and may include irrelevant rows; the reviewer must judge relevance.
A pending red-team prompt is not a judgment_review and cannot support an M6 decision.
No script-authored verdict or recommendation is permitted.
Priority weights allocate review attention only.
Later judgment must preserve Commander-first identity and bracket-specific context.

reviews.adversarial_challenge: Assume multiple permanent types are answered over several turns. Identify which strategic routes actually rebuild and which collapse after repeated removal.

value: No Narset/Notion Thief wheel locks (blueprint L59).
No Thassa's Oracle package (L60), no infect shortcuts (L61), no Mindcrank package (L62).

blueprint_failure_modes.description: A five-mana setup before the wheels; wheels without punishers refill opponents.
Opposing Narset/Notion Thief turn the deck off.

value.interaction: Free and cheap counters, Toxic Deluge, Cyclonic Rift.
value.mana: 35 lands, Mana Vault, Grim Monolith, Chrome Mox, Dark Ritual, Talismans; triple pips for Niv-Mizzet.

accepted_role.advances_plan: Nekusar is the best punisher and his draw-step trigger gives every opponent an extra draw to punish.
accepted_role.honest_note: The source says outright that without Nekusar the deck still works as a wheel/group-slug deck (blueprint L55) and that the punishers were chosen so it isn't commander-or-bust (L29). Only 1 of 7 Spellbook combos needs him (Nekusar + Peer into the Abyss). He multiplies the plan rather than being required by it. The cycle 51 M1 review (nekusar-01..09) verifies the engines and flags Krang self-damage (nekusar-03).
